ei.title: Law as a Reflection of Everyday Life
ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: Along with the mistaken notion that the law resides in the books goes the equally mistaken idea that law is secret, or at least inaccessible to the ordinary person. To understand and apply the law at the advanced, technical level that lawyers do requires professional knowledge, but to understand the basic substance of the law does not. Law reflects life. The principles and issues embodied in the law are not different from those that we experience in other aspects of our lives. Contract law, for example, is a commentary on the way people make, interpret, keep, and break their promises in commercial and noncommercial settings. Few nonlawyers can describe the objective theory of contract formation or the Statute of Frauds, but they have thought a lot about contracts and promises. If you cross your fingers when you make a promise, does it mean that the promise doesn't count? If your newly purchased television doesn't work, can you return it to the store? And so on.

❌ ④ embodied — principles and issues embodied in the law에서 과거분사 후치수식. 적절 ✅

❌ ① 원문 일치: the mistaken notion that the law resides in the books — 잘못된 관념
❌ ② 원문 일치: to understand the basic substance of the law does not [require professional knowledge]
✅ ③ 원문과 반대: principles and issues embodied in the law are not different from those that we experience → 법의 원칙은 일상과 다르지 않다. '무관하다'는 불일치 ←정답
❌ ④ 원문 일치: they have thought a lot about contracts and promises
det.tip: are not different from those that we experience in other aspects of our lives — 다르지 않다 ≠ 무관하다

ch: 법이 책 속에 있다는 관념은 잘못된 것이다.
법의 기본적인 본질을 이해하는 데 전문 지식은 필요하지 않다.
비법률가들도 계약과 약속에 대해 많이 생각해 왔다.

questions.passage: Along with the mistaken notion that the law resides in the books goes the equally mistaken idea that law is secret, or at least inaccessible to the ordinary person. To understand and apply the law at the advanced, technical level that lawyers do requires professional knowledge, but to understand the basic substance of the law does not. Law reflects life. The principles and issues embodied in the law are not different from those that we experience in other aspects of our lives. Contract law, for example, is a commentary on the way people make, interpret, keep, and break their promises in commercial and noncommercial settings. Few nonlawyers can describe the objective theory of contract formation or the Statute of Frauds, but they have thought a lot about contracts and promises. If you cross your fingers when you ①<u>make a promise</u>, does it mean that the promise ②<u>don't count</u>? If your newly ③<u>purchased</u> television doesn't work, can you ④<u>return</u> it to the store? And so on.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 주어 the promise(단수)에 doesn't가 와야 하는데 don't(복수)는 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① make a promise — you make a promise에서 2인칭 주어 + 동사원형. 적절 ✅
✅ ② don't count — 원문은 doesn't count. the promise(3인칭 단수) + doesn't count. don't는 복수 주어에 사용하므로 부적절 ←정답
❌ ③ purchased — newly purchased television에서 과거분사 수식. 적절 ✅
❌ ④ return — can you return에서 조동사 can + 동사원형. 적절 ✅
det.tip: 3인칭 단수: the promise doesn't count (don't ✕)
